title: Splitting and uniqueness for a derived triangle with separated degrees
statement: Let $R$ be a ring and let $D(R)$ be the derived category of $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $K,L\in D(R)$, and suppose that $L$ is isomorphic in $D(R)$ to a bounded complex of projective $R$-modules whose terms vanish outside degrees $[a,b]$. If $H^i(K)=0$ for all $i\geq a$, then $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(L,K)=0$. If $H^i(K)=0$ for all $i\geq a+1$, then every distinguished triangle $K\to M\to L\to K[1]$ splits as an isomorphism $M\cong K\oplus L$ compatible with the triangle; when $H^i(K)=0$ for all $i\geq a$, this splitting is unique.

source.place: Tag 0BCG, More on Algebra, Lemma splitting-unique

proof.text: Choose a bounded projective representative P^\bullet of L, with P^i=0 for i<a. Applying the precise vanishing lemma for bounded projective complexes [lem-pc-ring-precise-vanishing] to P^\bullet and a complex representing K gives Hom_{D(R)}(L,K)=0 whenever H^i(K)=0 for all i\geq a.

For a distinguished triangle K\to M\to L\xrightarrow{\delta}K[1], assume H^i(K)=0 for i\geq a+1. The shifted complex K[1] has H^i(K[1])=H^{i+1}(K)=0 for i\geq a, so the first step applied to the same projective representative of L gives Hom_{D(R)}(L,K[1])=0. Hence the connecting morphism \delta is zero.

source.place: Tag 0BCG, Lemma splitting-unique, proof of the splitting assertion

proof.text: The zero connecting morphism makes the triangle a biproduct triangle: the Mathlib split-triangle statement [lem-pc-derived-zero-third-split] gives an isomorphism M\cong K\oplus L compatible with the triangle.

source.place: Tag 0BCG, Lemma splitting-unique, proof of the splitting assertion

proof.text: If H^i(K)=0 for i\geq a, Step 1 gives Hom_{D(R)}(L,K)=0. For two compatible biproduct splittings, their composite fixes the K-summand and L-summand maps; subtracting the identity leaves a matrix with only an L\to K off-diagonal entry. That entry is zero by the Hom vanishing, so the composite is the identity and the splittings coincide.

source.place: Tag 0BCG, Lemma splitting-unique, proof of uniqueness

lean.statement: theorem derivedSplittingUnique (a b : ℤ) (K L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) (hL : ∃ P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ, (∀ i : ℤ, Projective (P.X i)) ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i → IsZero (P.X i)) ∧ Nonempty (L ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)) : ((∀ i : ℤ, a ≤ i → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K)) → ∀ f : L ⟶ K, f = 0) ∧ ((∀ i : ℤ, a + 1 ≤ i → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K)) → ∀ (M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R))), T.obj₁ = K → T.obj₂ = M → T.obj₃ = L → T ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) → ∃ e : T.obj₂ ≅ T.obj₁ ⊞ T.obj₃, T.mor₁ ≫ e.hom = biprod.inl ∧ T.mor₂ = e.hom ≫ biprod.snd) ∧ ((∀ i : ℤ, a ≤ i → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K)) → ∀ (M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R))), T.obj₁ = K → T.obj₂ = M → T.obj₃ = L → T ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) → ∀ (e₁ e₂ : T.obj₂ ≅ T.obj₁ ⊞ T.obj₃), T.mor₁ ≫ e₁.hom = biprod.inl → T.mor₂ = e₁.hom ≫ biprod.snd → T.mor₁ ≫ e₂.hom = biprod.inl → T.mor₂ = e₂.hom ≫ biprod.snd → e₁ = e₂)

reviewed_lean.note: R ring, D(ModuleCat R), K L, a b, hL projective complex zero outside [a,b] iso to L; (1) H^i K=0 i>=a -> Hom(L,K)=0; (2) i>=a+1 -> every dist. triangle K->M->L splits compatibly (mor1, mor2); (3) i>=a -> compatible splittings equal; fixed precedence so the three clauses are conjuncts
